title: A universal emulator for planar Ising lattices
authors: Riccardo Ben Alì Zinati, Alessandro Codello
abstract: We introduce the notion of an Ising emulator for two-dimensional Ising models: flat, unit-edge-length lattices can be represented as site- or bond-diluted supercells of a single host lattice, for which the Feynman--Vdovichenko/Kac--Ward solution is fixed once and for all. We construct explicit square and triangular emulators and show that a single transition matrix, supplemented by lattice-specific binary masks, gives all the thermodynamic quantities of interest for both ferro- and antiferromagnetic couplings. We apply the framework to all eleven Archimedean lattices, to all twenty $2$-uniform lattices -- whose thermodynamics is obtained here for the first time -- and to several pentagonal lattices, and show that the same construction extends directly to fractal and disordered Ising models, with no modification to the underlying machinery.
summary: This paper introduces an "Ising emulator," a universal computational framework that calculates the thermodynamics of diverse planar Ising lattices by representing them as dilutions of a single host lattice. By using the Feynman–Vdovichenko/Kac–Ward determinant, the authors demonstrate this method's power across numerous complex and disordered lattice geometries.
main_problem: To develop a universal computational framework (an "Ising emulator") for calculating thermodynamic properties of various planar Ising lattices.
main_result: The framework successfully applies to all eleven Archimedean lattices, twenty 2-uniform lattices, and extends directly to fractal and disordered Ising models using a single underlying machinery.
method: It represents any target lattice ($\Lambda$) as a site or bond dilution of a fixed host lattice ($\mathcal{H}$), allowing thermodynamic calculations via the Feynman–Vdovichenko/Kac–Ward determinant formula.
model_or_system: The system is the two-dimensional Ising model on planar lattices. The analysis uses an emulator approach by embedding the target lattice into a regular host (square or triangular) to calculate partition functions and thermodynamic quantities.
key_observables: Free energy, critical temperature ($T_c$), specific heat, entropy, and internal energy per spin.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), coupling constants ($\epsilon_c$, $\epsilon_{AF}$), and lattice structure/size parameters (e.g., $L$).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that thermodynamic properties are invariant under continuous topological deformations, allowing the use of a fixed host lattice for all calculations.
figures_summary: The notes indicate the presence of large, structured tables comparing calculated physical properties (Free energy, Specific heat $w(i)$, etc.) across numerous specific lattice types and sizes.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the emulator concept using the FV/KW method, details the construction for different hosts ($\square$ vs $	riangle$), applies this framework systematically to various classes of lattices (Archimedean, 2-uniform), and presents results in comparative tables across multiple lattice configurations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the concept of using a fixed 'host' structure with variable masks to model complex systems is analogous to defining effective Hamiltonians or transfer matrices in open quantum systems or quantum simulation contexts.
